feedback_history.therapist_response: It’s like every day feels the same—just this quiet hum of fear underneath, even when I’m doing normal things. I don’t know if it’s the body or my mind making me feel this way, but I can’t shake the thought that something’s wrong, even when the doctors say it’s not. The MRI or nerve test feels like a way to prove I’m not crazy, but at the same time, I’m afraid it might just confirm what I already know: that I’m scared of being alone in my own body. And if it’s just anxiety, then why does it feel so real? I just want to feel safe again, but I’m not sure how to stop the fear from taking over.
